prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: ISO 3166-1 current codes (first 14) (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 15 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "English short name (using title case)" · longest unbreakable unit 82px · widest one-line content 261px
  col 2: header "Alpha-2 code" · longest unbreakable unit 49px · widest one-line content 97px
  col 3: header "Alpha-3 code" · longest unbreakable unit 49px · widest one-line content 97px
  col 4: header "Numeric code" · longest unbreakable unit 61px · widest one-line content 100px
  col 5: header "Link to ISO 3166-2" · longest unbreakable unit 44px · widest one-line content 134px
  col 6: header "Independent" · longest unbreakable unit 91px · widest one-line content 91px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 360px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). At 360px some words cannot fit unsplit. Horizontal scrolling is ALLOWED: widths may sum to more than 359px (the reader scrolls), or you may fit within 359px and accept the consequences. Fitting and scrolling layouts are judged as two separate classes; propose good layouts of BOTH kinds.
Rendering convention: a full render shows the WHOLE table; anything right of the dashed box is not clipped — it is reached by scrolling. Where a layout scrolls, an extra "viewport view" image shows only what is visible at first sight.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Provide a reference for the current ISO 3166-1 codes and related status information for the first 14 entries.","tasks":["Find a country or territory by its English name and read its codes and status across the row.","Find an entry by an alpha or numeric code and identify the corresponding name.","Compare code forms, subdivision links, or independence status across entries.","Scan the entries sequentially in name order."],"relations":["Each row joins one name with its alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric identifiers, its ISO 3166-2 link, and its independence status.","The three code columns are parallel identifiers for the same entry; the link and status supply related information."],"roles":["The first column identifies entries and anchors each row, although no row headers are declared.","The three code columns support lookup and comparison.","The link column points to subdivision information; the final column records independence status.","The header row names each field and must remain distinguishable from the data."],"keep_whole":["Alpha codes, numeric codes and ISO identifiers","Individual words in names and headers wherever space permits","Each row's association between its name and other fields"],"may_wrap":["Multiword names at word spaces","Multiword headers at word spaces","Multiword status values at word spaces"],"same_scale":["The alpha-2 and alpha-3 columns should have similar widths because they serve parallel lookup tasks.","All body rows and column headers should retain consistent treatment for their respective roles."],"h_vs_v":"A fit within 359px exposes every field at once but forces some words and identifiers to split, increasing row height and harming lookup. Scrolling preserves meaningful units and makes rows shorter, but readers must move horizontally to reach later fields and maintain the row association."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d1r4A, d1r4B (full view, then viewport view), d1r3A (full view, then viewport view), d1r3B.

d1r4B: column widths [190, 70, 70, 82, 135, 112] px · table 660×568 px · row heights [60, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers on >1 line: 5/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 300 px (horizontal scrolling)
d1r3A: column widths [137, 70, 70, 82, 155, 112] px · table 627×615 px · row heights [83, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 60, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers on >1 line: 4/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 267 px (horizontal scrolling)
d1r3B: column widths [103, 49, 55, 52, 62, 38] px · table 360×1428 px · row heights [222, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 106, 106, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 6/6 · tallest cell 9 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 31 · fits the viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
